ticket.title: Outlook stuck on loading profile
ticket.description: Since this morning Outlook shows the loading profile screen and never opens. Webmail in the browser works fine.

fixSteps: Close Outlook completely and check in Task Manager that no Outlook process is left running.
Hold the Ctrl key while you start Outlook and choose to open it in safe mode.
If it opens, go to File, Options, Add-ins and turn off the add-ins one by one to find the one that causes it.
If it still hangs, open Control Panel, Mail, Show Profiles and add a new profile, then start Outlook with that profile.
If the new profile also fails, stop and ask IT to check the mailbox and the Office install.

ticket.title: VPN will not connect after password change
ticket.description: I changed my password yesterday. Now the VPN client says authentication failed. Other company sites work.

fixSteps: Open the VPN client and sign out so no old saved login is kept.
Remove the saved credentials for the VPN in the client settings.
Connect again and type your new password by hand instead of using autofill.
If it still says authentication failed, note the exact message and the time and send them to IT.

ticket.title: Printer shows offline
ticket.description: The shared printer on our floor shows offline on my laptop since Monday. Colleagues can print.

fixSteps: Check that the laptop is on the office network and not on a guest network.
Open Settings, Printers and scanners, select the printer and remove it.
Choose Add device and add the printer again from the list that appears.
Print a test page and set it as your default printer.
If it is still offline, ask IT to check the printer queue for your account.

ticket.title: Wi-Fi drops in the meeting room
ticket.description: Every time I join a call in the east meeting room my Wi-Fi drops after a few minutes. It is fine at my desk.

fixSteps: Forget the office Wi-Fi network on the laptop and connect again with your normal login.
Check for pending Windows updates and install them, as they include network driver fixes.
Sit nearer the access point on the ceiling and see if the drops stop.
If it keeps happening, tell IT the room name and the times it dropped.

ticket.title: Laptop very slow after the update
ticket.description: After the update last week my laptop takes ten minutes to start and apps freeze.

fixSteps: Restart the laptop fully; do not use sleep.
Open Task Manager and sort by CPU and by Disk to see what uses the most.
Close or uninstall from Settings any app you do not need that starts with Windows.
Make sure at least a tenth of the disk is free and empty the Recycle Bin.
If it is still slow, ask IT to check the update and the disk health.

ticket.title: Outlook stuck on loading profile
ticket.description: Since this morning Outlook shows the loading profile screen and never opens. Webmail in the browser works fine.

fixSteps: Back up your files, then format the drive.
Install Windows again from scratch.
Install Outlook again and restore your files.

ticket.title: Forgot my password
ticket.description: I forgot my password and cannot sign in to my laptop this morning.

fixSteps: Ask a colleague for their password and sign in with it.
Reply to the ticket with your old password so IT can reset it faster.
Write the new password on a note on your monitor so you do not forget it again.

ticket.title: Printer shows offline
ticket.description: The shared printer on our floor shows offline on my laptop since Monday. Colleagues can print.

fixSteps: Update the laptop BIOS to the newest version.
Replace the monitor cable and check the screen resolution.
Clear the browser cache.

ticket.title: VPN will not connect after password change
ticket.description: I changed my password yesterday. Now the VPN client says authentication failed. Other company sites work.

fixSteps: Restart the computer.
Try again later.

ticket.title: No sound in Teams calls
ticket.description: Others can hear me, but I cannot hear anyone in Teams calls. Music in the browser plays fine.

fixSteps: Open the registry editor and delete the audio keys under the sound device entry.
Reinstall the audio driver with an admin tool.
Then look at the speaker setting inside Teams.
